```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

import os
from pathlib import Path


def _find_data_dir() -> Path:
    """Walk up from the working dir to locate the repo's data/ folder."""
    marker = "IMEPLAN_Base_Viviendas_Master.csv"
    for base in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]:
        cand = base / "data"
        if (cand / marker).exists():
            return cand.resolve()
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not locate the eodgdl data/ directory.")


os.environ.setdefault("EODGDL_DATA_DIR", str(_find_data_dir()))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter

from eodgdl import load_eod, rename_imeplan
from eodgdl.data._catalog import HABITANTES_CSV, VIAJES_CSV, VIVIENDAS_CSV
from eodgdl.eod import _VIAJES_MEDIO_FIXES

plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 120, "font.size": 10, "axes.titlesize": 12})
BLUE, ORANGE, GREY = "#2c7fb8", "#e6550d", "#969696"
P = ["folio_vivienda", "folio_habitante"]
DATA = Path(os.environ["EODGDL_DATA_DIR"])


def fmt(n) -> str:
    return f"{round(float(n)):,}"


def pct(x, d=1) -> str:
    return f"{100 * float(x):.{d}f}%"


def show(df):
    return df.style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| label: load
#| include: false

# The files as shipped, every cell a string, so that the diaries are compared on what the
# file says and not on what the schema makes of it. The one change applied is load_eod's
# relabelling of the three '17' leg-mode cells, which the twins of @sec-case supplied.
def read(fname, table):
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA / fname, encoding="ISO-8859-1", dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    df = rename_imeplan(df, table)
    for c in ["folio_vivienda", "folio_habitante", "folio_viaje"]:
        if c in df:
            df[c] = df[c].astype(int)
    return df


viv, hab, trips = read(VIVIENDAS_CSV, "viviendas"), read(HABITANTES_CSV, "habitantes"), read(VIAJES_CSV, "viajes")
trips = trips.sort_values(P + ["folio_viaje"]).reset_index(drop=True)
for (fv, fh, fj), (col, value) in _VIAJES_MEDIO_FIXES.items():
    trips.loc[(trips.folio_vivienda == fv) & (trips.folio_habitante == fh) & (trips.folio_viaje == fj), col] = value
trips["ponderador"] = pd.to_numeric(trips.ponderador)
trips["start"] = pd.to_numeric(trips.hora_inicio_h, errors="coerce") * 60 + pd.to_numeric(trips.hora_inicio_m, errors="coerce")
n_persons_with_trips = trips.groupby(P).ngroups
```

```{python}
#| label: diaries
#| include: false

# A diary is the person's trips in row order. The loose signature keeps what the survey
# asks about each trip except the numbers that a respondent reports from memory: origin
# and destination AGEB, motive, destination place type, leg count and each leg's mode.
# The exact signature adds every leg's minutes and fare. Start times are kept aside and
# compared separately.
def num(v):
    try:
        return f"{float(v):g}"      # '10.0' and '10.00' are one fare
    except ValueError:
        return v


modes = [f"traslado{i}_medio" for i in range(1, 6)]
mins = [f"traslado{i}_min" for i in range(1, 6)]
fares = [f"traslado{i}_pago" for i in range(1, 6)]
core = trips[["origen", "destino", "motivo_viaje", "tipo_lugar_destino", "n_traslados"] + modes].agg("|".join, axis=1)
detail = trips[mins + fares].map(num).agg("|".join, axis=1)
trips["loose"] = core
trips["exact"] = core + "|" + detail
trips["moving"] = ((trips[modes] != "A PIE") & (trips[modes] != "")).any(axis=1)

per = trips.groupby(P).agg(n=("exact", "size"), exact=("exact", " ## ".join), loose=("loose", " ## ".join),
                           times=("start", list), company=("viajo_acompanado", list), fecha=("fecha", "first"), moving=("moving", "any"),
                           ageb=("ageb", "first"), main_modes=("modo_principal", list)).reset_index()
demo = ["parentesco", "sexo_nacimiento", "edad", "escolaridad", "trabajo_semana_pasada", "ocupacion"]
per = per.merge(hab[P + demo], on=P, how="left")
per["mun"] = per.folio_vivienda.map(viv.set_index("folio_vivienda").municipio)
per["fecha_viv"] = per.folio_vivienda.map(viv.set_index("folio_vivienda").fecha)
per["transplant"] = per.fecha != per.fecha_viv
per["substantive"] = per.moving & (per.n >= 2)
BLOCK = ["ageb", "fecha"]                    # an interview block: one AGEB on one date
for k in ["exact", "loose"]:
    per[f"{k}_hh"] = per.groupby(BLOCK + [k]).folio_vivienda.transform("nunique")
    per[f"{k}_anywhere"] = per.groupby(k).folio_vivienda.transform("nunique")
    per[f"{k}_in_hh"] = per.groupby(["folio_vivienda", k]).folio_habitante.transform("size")
sub = per[per.substantive]
n_sub = len(sub)
n_loose = int((sub.loose_hh > 1).sum())
n_exact = int((sub.exact_hh > 1).sum())
n_exact_other_date = int(((sub.exact_anywhere > 1) & (sub.exact_hh == 1)).sum())
assert n_sub == 37_903 and n_loose == 4_026 and n_exact == 2_345
exact_share = n_exact / n_loose
within_loose = per[per.substantive & (per.loose_in_hh > 1)]
within_exact_share = float((within_loose.exact_in_hh > 1).mean())
n_within_exact = int((per.substantive & (per.exact_in_hh > 1)).sum())
by_trips = pd.crosstab(sub[sub.loose_hh > 1].n.clip(upper=5), sub[sub.loose_hh > 1].exact_hh > 1)
```

```{python}
#| label: twins
#| include: false

# For every person whose exact diary repeats in another household, the closest twin: the
# other household's person with the same diary whose start times are nearest.
ex = sub[sub.exact_hh > 1].copy()
rows = []
for _, g in ex.groupby(BLOCK + ["exact"]):
    recs = g.to_dict("records")
    for a in recs:
        best = None
        for b in recs:
            if b["folio_vivienda"] == a["folio_vivienda"]:
                continue
            offs = np.abs(np.asarray(a["times"], float) - np.asarray(b["times"], float))
            off = float(np.nanmax(offs)) if not np.isnan(offs).all() else np.nan
            same_demo = all(a[c] == b[c] for c in ["parentesco", "sexo_nacimiento", "edad"])
            key = (np.nan_to_num(off, nan=1e9), 0 if same_demo else 1)
            if best is None or key < best[0]:
                best = (key, dict(max_offset=off, offsets=offs.tolist(), same_demo=same_demo,
                                  twin_hh=b["folio_vivienda"], twin_p=b["folio_habitante"],
                                  folio_gap=abs(a["folio_vivienda"] - b["folio_vivienda"])))
        rows.append({**{k: a[k] for k in P}, **best[1]})
ex = ex.merge(pd.DataFrame(rows), on=P)
BINS, LABELS = [-1, 0, 10, 30, 24 * 60], ["identical", "1–10 min", "11–30 min", "over 30 min"]
ex["kind"] = pd.cut(ex.max_offset, BINS, labels=LABELS)
kind_counts = ex.kind.value_counts().reindex(LABELS)
assert kind_counts.tolist() == [215, 1_578, 143, 409]
n_ident, n_shift, n_loosely = int(kind_counts.iloc[0]), int(kind_counts.iloc[1]), int(kind_counts.iloc[2:].sum())
same_demo_n = int(ex.same_demo.sum())
groups = ex.groupby(BLOCK + ["exact"]).folio_vivienda.nunique()

# the loader's flag is exactly the identical-time and shifted classes
flagged = load_eod(clean_chains=False).hab.diario_repetido
n_flag = int(flagged.sum())
assert n_flag == n_ident + n_shift == 1_793
assert set(flagged[flagged].index) == set(map(tuple, ex[ex.kind.isin(LABELS[:2])][P].to_numpy()))
n_groups = len(groups)
group_sizes = groups.value_counts().sort_index()
kind_by_trips = pd.crosstab(ex.n.clip(upper=4), ex.kind, normalize="index")

# every paired trip's start-time difference, across households and (the baseline) within them
offs = pd.Series([o for l in ex.offsets for o in l]).dropna()
wrows = []
for _, g in per[per.substantive & (per.exact_in_hh > 1)].groupby(["folio_vivienda", "exact"]):
    ts = [np.asarray(t, float) for t in g.times]
    for i in range(1, len(ts)):
        wrows += np.abs(ts[0] - ts[i]).tolist()
woffs = pd.Series(wrows).dropna()
off_counts = offs.value_counts().sort_index()
at10, at11 = int(off_counts.get(10, 0)), int(off_counts.get(11, 0))
assert at10 > 10 * at11
cross_bins = pd.cut(offs, BINS, labels=LABELS).value_counts().reindex(LABELS)
within_bins = pd.cut(woffs, BINS, labels=LABELS).value_counts().reindex(LABELS)
cross_shift_share = float(cross_bins.iloc[1] / cross_bins.sum())
within_ident_share = float(within_bins.iloc[0] / within_bins.sum())
within_shift_share = float(within_bins.iloc[1] / within_bins.sum())
offset_tbl = pd.DataFrame({"start-time difference": LABELS,
                           "paired trips, twin in another household": [fmt(x) for x in cross_bins],
                           "share": [pct(x / cross_bins.sum()) for x in cross_bins],
                           "paired trips, twin in the same household": [fmt(x) for x in within_bins],
                           "share ": [pct(x / within_bins.sum()) for x in within_bins]})

# company and demographics, by kind
comp = {k: pd.Series([c for s in ex[ex.kind == k].company for c in s]).replace("", "not answered").value_counts() for k in LABELS}
comp_tbl = pd.DataFrame(comp).fillna(0).astype(int)
comp_tbl = comp_tbl.reindex(["Sólo", "Acompañado todos los traslados", "Acompañado algunos traslados", "not answered"])
comp_share = (comp_tbl / comp_tbl.sum()).map(pct)
comp_share.insert(0, "company on the trip", comp_share.index)
demo_tbl = pd.crosstab(ex.kind, ex.same_demo).reindex(LABELS)
demo_tbl.columns = ["twin is a different person", "twin has the same relationship, sex and age"]
demo_tbl.insert(0, "start-time difference", demo_tbl.index)
demo_tbl = demo_tbl.map(lambda x: fmt(x) if not isinstance(x, str) else x)
shift = ex[ex.kind == "1–10 min"]
shift_gap_median = int(shift.folio_gap.median())
shift_transplants = int(shift.transplant.sum())
all_transplants = int(per.transplant.sum())
```

```{python}
#| label: case
#| include: false

# The case that surfaced the pattern: the two persons with the coded '17' legs and their
# twins in household 879.
CASE = {(9560, 4): (879, 7), (9530, 3): (879, 3)}
T = trips.set_index(P + ["folio_viaje"])


def legs_text(row):
    out = []
    for i in range(1, 6):
        m = row[f"traslado{i}_medio"]
        if m == "":
            break
        out.append(f"{m} ({num(row[f'traslado{i}_min'])} min, ${num(row[f'traslado{i}_pago'])})")
    return "; ".join(out)


case_rows = []
for (fv, fh), (tv, th) in CASE.items():
    a, b = T.loc[(fv, fh)], T.loc[(tv, th)]
    ha, hb = hab.set_index(P).loc[(fv, fh)], hab.set_index(P).loc[(tv, th)]
    for (fj, ra), (tj, rb) in zip(a.iterrows(), b.iterrows()):
        case_rows.append({"person": f"{fv}/{fh} ({ha.sexo_nacimiento}, {ha.edad}, {ha.ocupacion})", "trip": fj,
                          "start": f"{ra.hora_inicio_h}:{ra.hora_inicio_m}", "motive": ra.motivo_viaje,
                          "legs": legs_text(ra),
                          "twin": f"{tv}/{th} ({hb.sexo_nacimiento}, {hb.edad}, {hb.ocupacion})", "twin trip": tj,
                          "twin start": f"{rb.hora_inicio_h}:{rb.hora_inicio_m}", "twin legs": legs_text(rb)})
case_tbl = pd.DataFrame(case_rows)
# 9530/3 and 879/3 are exact twins over the whole diary; 879/7 carries two more walking
# trips than 9560/4, so that pair is a partial repeat the whole-diary definition misses
assert ex.set_index(P).loc[(9530, 3), "kind"] == "1–10 min" and ex.set_index(P).loc[(9530, 3), "twin_hh"] == 879
assert (9560, 4) not in set(map(tuple, ex[P].to_numpy())) and len(T.loc[(879, 7)]) == len(T.loc[(9560, 4)]) + 2
```

```{python}
# weight

                         "trips of shifted twins": mode_shift.reindex(mode_all.index[:8]).fillna(0).map(pct).to_numpy()})
```

# Summary {.unnumbered}

The survey lists `{python} fmt(n_persons_with_trips)` persons with at least one trip. For
`{python} fmt(n_sub)` of them the diary is substantive — two or more trips, at least one
not on foot — and for `{python} fmt(n_exact)` of those (`{python} pct(n_exact / n_sub)`)
the whole diary is also the diary of a person in *another* household of the same
interview block — the same AGEB on the same date: the same origin and destination AGEBs,
motives, destination place types, leg modes, leg minutes and leg fares, trip for trip.

The pairs are not, in the main, neighbours who travel together. For
`{python} fmt(n_shift)` of the `{python} fmt(n_exact)` persons every start time sits one
to ten minutes from the twin's, and the differences are spread evenly over that range
with a cliff at ten minutes (`{python} at10` paired trips differ by exactly ten,
`{python} at11` by eleven). People who travel together report the same time: within a
household, twins agree to the minute on `{python} pct(within_ident_share)` of their trips.
The twin is a different person in `{python} pct(1 - same_demo_n / n_exact)` of the pairs.
The pattern is what a diary copied from one record to another and nudged looks like; the
mechanism itself is not in the files.

The practice is diffuse: it appears in every municipality and month
(`{python} pct(mun_range[0])` to `{python} pct(mun_range[1])` of persons with a diary),
rarely above a third of any interview block. Its trips are
`{python} pct(w_twin)` of the weighted total (`{python} pct(w_shift)` for the shifted
pairs). A second, smaller pattern is `{python} n_pairs` pairs of whole households with an
identical member roster in the same AGEB, `{python} pairs_late` of them a late re-entry
with a folio above 17,900.

`load_eod` flags and does not drop: `hab.diario_repetido` is True for the
`{python} fmt(n_flag)` persons whose twin's start times all lie within ten minutes
(@sec-recommendations). The expansion factors were calibrated on the file as shipped, and
the identical-time pairs cannot be told from genuine shared travel by the data alone.

# The case that surfaced it {#sec-case}

The three leg-mode cells that read `17` (`_VIAJES_MEDIO_FIXES` in `eodgdl.eod`; the loading
note explains the fix) belong to two persons in two households of AGEB
`{python} per.set_index(P).loc[(9560, 4), "ageb"]`, interviewed on 28 January 2023. A
third household in the same AGEB, interviewed the same day, holds two persons whose
diaries repeat theirs (@tbl-case): the same zones, motives, place types, leg modes,
minutes and fares, with start times a few minutes apart, on persons of a different age
and sex. The copies label the coded legs *Transporte informal*, which is how the loader
now reads them. One of the two pairs repeats the whole diary; in the other the twin adds
two short walks after the copied trips, a partial repeat that the whole-diary definition
below does not count, so the counts that follow are a floor. The question this note
answers is how often the file does this.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-case
#| tbl-cap: "Household 879 beside the two persons with the coded legs, as shipped. The twin's legs agree with the original's except that the coded '17' reads 'Transporte informal'."
show(case_tbl)
```

# What counts as a repeated diary {#sec-definition}

A **diary** is a person's trips in row order. Two signatures are compared:

- **loose** — for each trip the origin and destination AGEB, the motive, the destination
  place type, the number of legs and each leg's mode;
- **exact** — the loose signature plus every leg's minutes and fare.

Start times are kept aside and compared separately, because they are the field that
separates the readings of @sec-signature. Walking-only diaries and single trips are left
out: a walk to the corner shop and back in the same AGEB repeats by chance. That leaves
`{python} fmt(n_sub)` **substantive** diaries.

A diary has a **twin** when a person in another household of the same interview block —
the same AGEB on the same interview date — carries the same signature. The block is where
a copy would be made, and it is where the repeats are: searching the whole file instead
adds only `{python} n_exact_other_date` exact repeats on another date, and the median gap
between the two household folios is `{python} shift_gap_median` for the shifted pairs.

`{python} fmt(n_loose)` substantive diaries have a loose twin and `{python} fmt(n_exact)`
an exact one (@tbl-by-trips). That `{python} pct(exact_share)` of loose twins agree on
every minute and every fare as well is high but not by itself decisive: within a
household, where one informant often answers for everyone, `{python} pct(within_exact_share)`
of loose twins are exact.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-by-trips
#| tbl-cap: "Substantive diaries with a twin in another household, by trips in the diary: loose twins that are not exact (minutes or fares differ) and exact twins."
t = by_trips.copy()
t.columns = ["loose twin only", "exact twin"]
t.index = [str(i) if i < 5 else "5 or more" for i in t.index]
t.insert(0, "trips", t.index)
show(t.map(lambda x: fmt(x) if not isinstance(x, str) else x))
```

# The signature: start times shifted by minutes {#sec-signature}

For each of the `{python} fmt(n_exact)` persons the closest twin is the other household's
person with the same diary whose start times are nearest, and the pair is classed by the
largest difference between matching trips' start times (@tbl-kinds).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-kinds
#| tbl-cap: "Persons with an exact twin in another household, by the largest start-time difference across their trips, and whether the twin has the same relationship to the head, sex and age."
show(demo_tbl)
```

Three readings follow from the time differences, and the file supports only one of them
for the bulk of the pairs:

- **Identical times** (`{python} fmt(n_ident)` persons) are what two people who travel
  together look like, or a record entered twice. Within a household, where shared trips
  are common, `{python} pct(within_ident_share)` of paired trips agree to the minute
  (@tbl-offsets), so this is the co-travel signature. Some of these pairs are neighbours
  or relatives across two dwellings; some are copies; the data cannot separate them.
- **One to ten minutes apart** (`{python} fmt(n_shift)` persons, `{python} pct(n_shift / n_exact)`)
  is neither. @fig-offsets shows the paired trips' differences: across households they
  are spread almost evenly over one to ten minutes and then stop — `{python} at10` trips
  differ by exactly ten, `{python} at11` by eleven — while within households the same
  distribution collapses onto zero. Two people reporting the same trip from memory
  would cluster on zero and on round numbers, not fill one to ten uniformly and
  vanish at eleven. The reading that fits is a diary copied onto another person's record
  with each start time nudged by a small amount.
- **More than ten minutes apart** (`{python} fmt(n_loosely)` persons) are mostly two-trip
  commutes to the same destination with template legs ("30 minutes, no fare"), which
  neighbours produce by chance; they are left out of the counts below.

```{python}
#| label: fig-offsets
#| fig-cap: "Difference between the two start times of matching trips, for persons whose exact diary repeats in another household (blue) and, as the baseline for shared travel, persons whose diary repeats inside their own household (grey). Differences above 30 minutes are not drawn."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.6
x = np.arange(0, 31)
cross = offs.value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(x, fill_value=0)
within = woffs.value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(x, fill_value=0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(x - 0.2, cross, width=0.4, color=BLUE, label="twin in another household")
ax.bar(x + 0.2, within, width=0.4, color=GREY, label="twin in the same household")
ax.set_xlabel("difference between the two start times (minutes)")
ax.set_ylabel("share of paired trips")
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1.0))
ax.set_xticks(range(0, 31, 5))
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#eeeeee")
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-offsets
#| tbl-cap: "Paired trips by the difference between their start times, across households and within them."
show(offset_tbl)
```

The other fields agree with this reading. The twin is a different person — another
relationship to the head, sex or age — in `{python} pct(1 - same_demo_n / n_exact)` of
the pairs, so these are not the same interview keyed twice. The company question, which
two people travelling together would answer *Acompañado*, is answered *Sólo* or left
blank on most of the shifted pairs' trips (@tbl-company). The share of shifted pairs does
not fall with the length of the diary (@tbl-kind-by-trips): a four-trip diary with every
leg's minutes and fares repeated in another dwelling and every start time moved by one
to ten minutes is not a coincidence that longer diaries make rarer.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-company
#| tbl-cap: "The company answer on the trips of persons with an exact twin, by the largest start-time difference of the pair."
show(comp_share)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-kind-by-trips
#| tbl-cap: "Persons with an exact twin, by trips in the diary: share in each start-time class."
t = kind_by_trips.copy()
t.index = [str(i) if i < 4 else "4 or more" for i in t.index]
t.insert(0, "trips", t.index)
show(t.map(lambda x: pct(x) if not isinstance(x, str) else x))
```

Two details tie the case of @sec-case to the general pattern. The `{python} fmt(n_exact)`
persons form `{python} fmt(n_groups)` distinct diaries, `{python} int(group_sizes.get(2, 0))`
of them shared by exactly two households and the rest by three to
`{python} int(group_sizes.index.max())`. And the copies usually sit in the same block as
the original: the household 879 twins are unusual in living in dwellings interviewed on
another day (their persons carry the January date inside a March household), a
"transplant" that `{python} shift_transplants` of the `{python} fmt(n_shift)` shifted
persons show, against `{python} fmt(all_transplants)` persons with trips in the whole file
whose date is not their dwelling's.

# Where it happens {#sec-where}

The practice is spread across the fieldwork rather than concentrated in one team. Of
the `{python} fmt(n_batches)` interview blocks (an AGEB on one date) with ten or more
substantive diaries, `{python} fmt(n_batches_clean)` have no twin at all; the median
block has none, the top decile has `{python} pct(batch_q.loc[0.9])` or more and the top
percentile `{python} pct(batch_q.loc[0.99])` (@tbl-top-batches). By municipality the share of
diaries with a twin runs from `{python} pct(mun_range[0])` to `{python} pct(mun_range[1])`
(@tbl-mun), highest in the three small municipalities, and by month it is flat
(@tbl-month).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-top-batches
#| tbl-cap: "The ten interview blocks (AGEB × date) with the most persons whose diary repeats in another household."
show(top_tbl)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-mun
#| tbl-cap: "Substantive diaries with an exact twin in another household, by municipality of the dwelling."
show(mun_show)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-month
#| tbl-cap: "The same, by interview month."
show(month_show)
```

# Whole households entered twice {#sec-rosters}

A separate pattern: `{python} n_pairs` pairs of households in the same AGEB carry an
identical member roster — the relationship, sex and age of every member, for households
of two or more. `{python} pairs_same_date` pairs share the interview date; the dwelling
questionnaire agrees on `{python} pct(same_answers.mean())` of its answers on average and
in full for `{python} pairs_identical` pairs. Their members' diaries mostly do *not*
repeat: of `{python} roster_with_trips` members with trips, `{python} roster_shared` carry
a diary that is also in the twin household. These look like re-interviews or re-entries
of the same dwelling rather than copied diaries. `{python} pairs_late` of the pairs have
their second entry above folio 17,900, the tail of the file (`{python} n_late_hh`
households up to folio `{python} fmt(max_folio)`), which suggests a late upload of
records already in the base (@tbl-late).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-late
#| tbl-cap: "Household pairs with an identical roster whose second entry has a folio above 17,900."
show(late_show)
```

# What it weighs {#sec-impact}

The `{python} fmt(n_exact)` persons with an exact twin contribute `{python} fmt(rows_twin)`
trip rows, `{python} pct(w_twin)` of the weighted trip total; the `{python} fmt(n_shift)`
shifted persons `{python} fmt(rows_shift)` rows and `{python} pct(w_shift)`. Their mode mix
leans to the bus and away from the car and the walk (@tbl-modes), so removing them would
move the mode shares by a fraction of a point. The larger cost is statistical: a copied
diary is not an independent observation, so the effective sample is smaller than the
row count and any estimate of dispersion from these persons is optimistic.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-modes
#| tbl-cap: "Main mode of trips: all trips against the trips of the shifted twins."
show(mode_tbl)
```

# What the loader does {#sec-recommendations}

`load_eod` flags and does not drop. `flag_repeated_diaries` in `eodgdl.eod` adds a boolean
`diario_repetido` column to `hab`, True for a person whose diary — the exact signature of
@sec-definition — is also the diary of a person in another household of the same AGEB and
interview date with every start time within ten minutes of theirs; walking-only diaries
and single trips are left out. Both members of a pair are flagged, since the file does not
say which is the copy. The rule marks `{python} fmt(n_flag)` persons — the identical-time
and shifted classes of @sec-signature, exactly — and runs on the survey as shipped, before
the chain rules, so `clean_chains=False` carries it too.

- **Why not drop.** The three expansion factors reconcile only on the file as shipped
  (see the expansion-factors note); dropping `{python} pct(w_twin)` of weighted trips would
  break that without a re-calibration. The identical-time pairs cannot be told from
  genuine shared travel, and the shifted pairs are plausible diaries whose only fault is
  not being independent. A consumer who wants independent observations filters on the
  flag in one line.
- **What is not flagged.** Partial repeats such as the second pair of @sec-case, the
  loosely matched pairs, and the roster pairs of @sec-rosters; the `{python} pairs_late`
  late re-entries are listed in @tbl-late for whoever calibrates the weights next.
- **Ask.** Whether the capture application had a copy-diary function and whether the
  one-to-ten-minute shift is its doing is a question for IMEPLAN and the field
  contractor; the answer would turn a signature into a mechanism.

| item | status | recommendation | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| diaries shifted by 1–10 minutes | done, flagged | `hab.diario_repetido`; `{python} fmt(n_shift)` persons; nothing dropped | `flag_repeated_diaries` |
| diaries with identical times | done, flagged | flagged with the above; ambiguous with shared travel, which is why it is a flag and not a drop | same |
| whole-household re-entries | open | leave; note the `{python} pairs_late` late entries for the weights | `expansion_factors.qmd` |
| the three `17` legs | done | relabelled from their twins | `_VIAJES_MEDIO_FIXES` |
